subject.title: Import Scrollmark and twitter-web-exporter captures into the canonical local store

question: Should third-party passive-capture files become a permanently supported Birdclaw import source, and what provenance, account-binding, collection-completeness, and initial format guarantees should that support commit to?
rationale: Existing code establishes canonical storage mechanics but cannot determine which external formats and durable semantic guarantees the product should maintain.

options.title: Approve Scrollmark v1 MVP
options.body: Support only the versioned Scrollmark canonical bundle initially, with explicit provenance and only semantically proven collection edges.

options.title: Approve broad compatibility
options.body: Support Scrollmark plus legacy JSON/JSONL and twitter-web-exporter shapes, accepting a substantially larger compatibility surface.

options.title: Defer external captures
options.body: Keep official archives, Birdclaw backups, and live transports as the only supported ingestion sources for now.

recommendation.title: Approve Scrollmark v1 MVP
recommendation.body: Support only the versioned Scrollmark canonical bundle initially, with explicit provenance and only semantically proven collection edges.

likelyOwner.reason: He is identified as Birdclaw’s product owner and is the strongest available owner for selecting the permanent import contract.
